blockers.description: Real correctness bug found in sim.js's existing applyAppraisal() (not new code from this phase): it hardcodes event.actor as the relational-consequence target (trust/affection/grievance/emotions/SeekRestitution goal). That's correct for Take/Attack/Give (the actor did it to you) but wrong for Tell (the actor is the messenger, not who the claim is about -- applyClaimBelief already correctly routes Tell's relational consequences to claim.subject, so applyAppraisal firing on Tell double-counts at the wrong target). This is what flipped Phase 1's positive-clone-attacks-player regression check: ives ends up attacking mara (the messenger who gossiped) instead of player (who actually attacked mara).
blockers.workaround: Confirmed fix via advisor consultation, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: give appraiseEvent's return shape a generic attributedTo field, defaulting to event.actor (unchanged behavior for Take/Attack/Give), explicitly null for Tell (and must also be null for Move's D-04 flight branch once 04-02 is written, same bug would otherwise recur). applyAppraisal reads appraisal.attributedTo instead of event.actor everywhere, and no-ops (skips all relational/emotional/goal work) when it's null/falsy -- impact still flows into addMemory() for memory-importance purposes since that happens earlier in perceiveEvent, unaffected by this fix.
